analysis.title: US Pulse: a gradual approach to monetary tightening
key_insights: ANZ expects the FOMC to raise rates by 25bp at the December meeting and by another 25bp in Q1 next year, after holding rates at the October meeting.

Advance Q3 GDP rose 3.4% annualised, up from 2.2% in Q2. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9% versus 4.6% in Q2. ANZ argues this demand strength is a reason the FOMC cannot leave rates on hold for much longer.

Consumption contributed 2.5ppt to Q3 GDP growth, with real consumption up 3.8% annualised, the same pace as Q2. NY Fed research indicates spending growth since 2023 has been driven disproportionately by higher-income households.

Gross private domestic investment rose 19.4% annualised in Q3 and added 3.3ppt to growth. Equipment investment rose 20.9%, the third straight quarter of double-digit growth, tied to the AI buildout and data-centre construction. Residential investment is constrained by high mortgage rates and affordability.

Net trade subtracted 3.3ppt from Q3 growth because of surging goods imports. Capital goods are at a record share of goods imports and consumer goods at a record low share, so part of the trade deficit reflects the AI investment boom.
ANZ says concentrated growth drivers leave the economy more exposed to a reversal in wealth-driven consumption or the AI investment cycle.

September PCE: headline +0.49% m/m (3.6% y/y), core +0.32% m/m (3.1% y/y). Core PCE rose 2.9% on a 3-month annualised basis, up from 2.2%. Market-based PCE rose 0.34% m/m from 0.24%, which ANZ reads as a reversal of recent disinflationary momentum.

September real consumer spending was flat (0.0% m/m) as nominal spending rose 0.5%. Real durable goods spending fell 0.8%, and motor vehicles fell 2.0%. Real disposable income fell 0.3% m/m and the savings rate fell to 3.8%, the lowest since October 2022.
The Conference Board consumer confidence index rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September. The share saying jobs are plentiful rose to 26.7% from 24.3%.

The October nonfarm payrolls report (due 7 Nov) is expected to show +65k versus 29k in September, with unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. The four-week average of initial claims is at its lowest since 1969, while labour demand and job openings remain soft.
ISM manufacturing is expected at 54.5 and ISM services at 54.8 (prior 54.9). ANZ notes persistent cost pressures across both sectors keep inflation risks elevated.
The preliminary University of Michigan sentiment index is expected at 48.0, a five-month low, held down by inflation, subdued hiring and high mortgage rates.

Republicans are widely expected to lose control of Congress at this week's midterm election. A Democratic clean sweep or divided Congress would point to policy gridlock and protracted budget negotiations.
Markets are being driven by concerns over big tech valuations and continued rapid AI infrastructure investment. The Fed is watching how this affects financial conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 GDP of 3.4% and final private domestic demand of 4.9% show a robust economy, driven by consumption and AI-related investment, which supports ANZ's call for rate increases in December and Q1.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth rests on concentrated drivers: higher-income household spending and the AI capex cycle. Real spending was flat in September, real disposable income fell and the savings rate is at its lowest since October 2022.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reversal in wealth-driven consumption or in the AI investment cycle, which ANZ says would expose the economy.
